correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs the exact two-band Fourier resolvent and the positive off-diagonal Neumann series; differentiates the inverse twice and proves strictness through the nonzero Bloch polynomial; bounds every periodic extra return by q^(2n); and derives the singular coefficient using an explicit matching resolvent and O(s²epsilon²) error. Positive-walk moments and an exact rational geometric-tail certificate enclose the isotropic root. The package verifier replayed 537 checks; finite checks are supplementary, not universal proofs.

originality.rationale: Compared mathematical implications rather than titles. The known generic return criterion, weighted closed-walk enumeration and isotropic/Dirichlet Green functions do not themselves assert the simultaneous sharp budget-normalized honeycomb allocation frontier, strict Schur ordering, finite-quotient error bound, and weak-matching root asymptotics. The original part lies in that joint analytic classification, not in Fourier transforms, inverse-positivity or generic matrix-inverse convexity. Specialist priority risk remains.
residual_risks: A specialized anisotropic honeycomb discretization paper not identified in the searched literature might independently establish the exact all-torus bound.
Abstract general matrix-inverse convexity combined with lattice symmetry is an available tool; the claimed novelty is not the abstract convexity lemma.
The weighted honeycomb closed-walk formalism already subsumes the isotropic moment sequence; no novelty is claimed for that sequence or for the spectral transform.
No independent human/expert mathematical review or exhaustive publication-priority certification has been performed.

value.rationale: Anisotropic three-direction honeycomb meshes and their toroidal approximations are natural semidiscrete diffusion models. The theorem yields the exact maximal nonnegativity timestep guaranteed simultaneously for all such grids with a fixed total rate, identifies the unique least-permissive allocation, quantifies finite-grid convergence and gives a universal degenerating-matching law. It resolves an exact design quantity not supplied by numerical-stability criteria or walk tables; its value does not rest on the small numerical gain over a coarse degree-only bound.
